title: Canvas 2D API
learningObjectives: Explain canvas 2d api and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: Canvas provides a bitmap drawing surface controlled through a 2D rendering context. JavaScript can draw paths, text, images, and shapes. Canvas pixels are not semantic DOM content, so provide accessible alternatives and account for device-pixel ratio when rendering sharply.
understand.whyItMatters: Canvas is useful for charts and visual tools but can be inaccessible if all information exists only as pixels. Use fallback text, summaries, and controls outside the canvas.
understand.analogy: Canvas is a drawing board; the DOM around it provides the labels and explanation that the painted pixels cannot communicate alone.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The code paints a rectangle and label into the canvas bitmap. A real chart should also provide a text summary or data table.

examples.explanation: The code paints a rectangle and label into the canvas bitmap. A real chart should also provide a text summary or data table.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Draw a simple bar chart and provide an equivalent accessible data summary in HTML.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: What does getContext('2d') return when supported?
questions.explanation: The 2D context provides drawing methods for the canvas bitmap.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
